claims.claim: The v0.11 memory allocator uses mem_map and get_free_page for page-level allocation; this is not a modern buddy allocator.
Modern page allocator organizes free memory into zones and buddy free areas; blocks are indexed by order and can split/coalesce.
SLUB became the default slab allocator in Linux 2.6.23; slab allocation manages objects on top of physical pages.
claims.locator: Make SLUB the default allocator commit
claims.notes: Compare upstream v2.6.22 init/Kconfig default SLAB with v2.6.23 default SLUB.

claims.claim: The fair scheduler evolved from CFS vruntime ordering toward EEVDF; EEVDF uses eligibility and virtual deadlines and is not the real-time deadline scheduling class.
Modern external modules use Kbuild; module_init and module_exit define module lifecycle hooks, while module code executes in kernel context.
Bounded eBPF loops have been supported since Linux 5.3; verifier complexity and safety checks still constrain programs.
XDP native, generic/SKB and hardware-offload paths have different driver/device requirements and expose defined XDP actions.
